questions.stem: Define the term unsaturated as applied to hydrocarbons.
questions.modelAnswer: An unsaturated hydrocarbon holds at least one carbon-carbon double bond that can open, letting additional atoms join the molecule by addition.

questions.stem: Name the first five members of the alkene series in order and give each formula.
questions.modelAnswer: Ethene C2H4, propene C3H6, but-1-ene C4H8, pent-1-ene C5H10, hex-1-ene C6H12.

questions.stem: Explain why propene and cyclopropane share the molecular formula C3H6.
questions.modelAnswer: Both structures lose the same hydrogen pair relative to propane C3H8: propene spends it on a carbon-carbon double bond while cyclopropane spends it closing a ring, so the two structural isomers share one formula.

questions.stem: A hydrocarbon is found with molecular formula C7H14. State whether it must be an open-chain alkene and justify your decision.
questions.modelAnswer: It need not be: C7H14 fits hept-1-ene (one double bond) but equally fits a cycloalkane such as methylcyclohexane, because one ring costs the same hydrogen pair as one double bond.

questions.stem: Describe how a sigma bond forms and state where its electron pair sits.
questions.modelAnswer: A sigma bond forms by end-on overlap of two orbitals, and the shared pair sits on the internuclear axis between the two nuclei.

questions.stem: State the three sigma bonds owned by each carbon atom inside an alkene unit.
questions.modelAnswer: Each alkene carbon holds two sigma bonds to its substituents and one sigma bond to the carbon of its double bond.

questions.stem: Explain why the framework around a C=C unit is planar rather than tetrahedral.
questions.modelAnswer: Each alkene carbon carries three sigma bonding regions and no lone pair, so the regions spread 120 degrees apart in a single plane; the fourth tetrahedral region is occupied by the pi bond instead of a sigma one.

questions.stem: Count the sigma and pi bonds in but-1-ene, CH2=CHCH2CH3.
questions.modelAnswer: Eight C-H sigma bonds plus three C-C sigma bonds give 11 sigma bonds, and the single double bond contributes one pi bond.

questions.stem: Describe the formation of a pi bond in ethene.
questions.modelAnswer: Sideways overlap of the unhybridised p orbitals on each alkene carbon builds a pi bond with electron density above and below the molecular plane.

questions.stem: State the two components of a carbon-carbon double bond and their electron counts.
questions.modelAnswer: The double bond holds one sigma pair from end-on overlap and one pi pair from sideways overlap - four shared electrons in total.

questions.stem: Explain why electrophiles are drawn to alkene molecules.
questions.modelAnswer: The pi cloud piles electron density above and below the plane where nothing shields it, so positive or electron-seeking species feel strong attraction and bond to the double-bond carbons.

questions.stem: Ethene carries 5 sigma bonds and 1 pi bond. Give the corresponding census for propene, C3H6.
questions.modelAnswer: Propene holds 8 sigma bonds - six to hydrogen and two along the carbon chain - and still exactly 1 pi bond at its double bond.
